Rashi on Sotah 46a:11:1.english: A yoke - [This] is taught with regard to the [red] heifer.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:11:2.english: Other [types of] labor disqualify it - For it is written: "with which no work has been done" [Deuteronomy 21:3].

Rashi on Sotah 46a:12:1.hebrew: ואם נפשך לומר - ואם יש לך להשיב על ק"ו זה, צא ולמד בג"ש: נאמר כאן עול כו':
Rashi on Sotah 46a:12:1.english: And if it is your wish to say - And if you have [an objection] to raise against this a fortiori inference, go and learn [it] through a verbal analogy: "It is stated here, 'yoke,'" etc.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:12:2.hebrew: נאמר כאן כו' - והאי עול יתירא הוא, דהא בכלל שאר עבודות הוא:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:12:2.english: It is stated here, etc. - And this [mention of] "yoke" is superfluous, for it is included in other labors.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:13:1.hebrew: מאי אם נפשך לומר - מאי הוה לך למיפרך, דשבקה תנא לאורחיה ויליף בגזירה שוה:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:13:1.english: What [is the meaning of] "If it is your wish to say" - What [objection] did you have to raise, that the Tanna abandoned his [usual] method and derived [it] through a verbal analogy?

Rashi on Sotah 46a:14:1.hebrew: וממקום שבאת - לאו תנא קתני לה, אלא תיובתיה קא מפרש ואזיל גמרא, דקא מותיב לרב יהודה דאמר לעיל שאר משאות פוסל בפרה בעלייה בעלמא. והא, כיון דשאר משאוי בפרה לא כתיב ומעגלה יליף לה בגזירה שוה, וממקום שבאת משם יש לך ללמד נמי, דמה עגלה עד שתמשוך, אף פרה בשאר משאות דילפינן מעגלה עד שתמשוך:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:14:1.english: And from the place that you came - The Tanna does not teach this; rather, the Gemara is proceeding to explain its refutation, as it is refuting Rav Yehudah, who said above [that] other burdens disqualify a [red] heifer merely by being placed upon [it]. Now, since other burdens are not written with regard to the [red] heifer, and [one] derives it from the [broken-necked] heifer through a verbal analogy, "and from the place that you came" — from there you must also learn that just as [with] the [broken-necked] heifer [it is not disqualified] until it pulls, so too [with] the [red] heifer regarding other burdens, which we derive from the [broken-necked] heifer, [it is not disqualified] until it pulls.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:16:1.hebrew: ת"ל אשר לא עלה עליה עול מ"מ - דריש ליה בלא עול מדלא כתיב אשר לא עלה עול עליה, ותו הדר כתיב עול לדרשא, כדדרשינא ואזיל:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:16:1.english: The verse states: “That upon which never came a yoke,” in any case - [The baraita] expounds it without [the word] “yoke,” since it is not written “upon which a yoke never came”; and then it writes “yoke” again for an exposition, as I go on to expound.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:18:1.hebrew: א"כ כו' שלא בשעת עבודה - ואפילו הניחו עליה להקל משא מידו, ולא למשוך:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:18:1.english: If so, etc., not at the time of labor - Even if he placed it upon it to lighten a burden from his hand, and not to pull.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:18:2.hebrew: אלא בשעת עבודה - כלומר, שעבודה זו לצורך היא, אבל אקראי בעלמא, שהניח שק עליה — ולא להוליכו אלא אקרי ואותיב — לא פסלה:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:18:2.english: Only at the time of labor - That is to say, that this labor is for a purpose; however, [if it is] merely incidental, where one placed a sack upon it — not to transport it, rather he happened to set [it down] — it does not disqualify it.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:1:1.hebrew: והכהנים אומרים - כדכתיב לעיל: ״ונגשו הכהנים בני לוי״, ולא פירש על מי הם נגשים:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:1:1.english: And the priests recite - As it is written earlier [in the Torah]: “And the priests, the sons of Levi, shall draw near” (Deuteronomy 21:5), and [Scripture] did not specify for whom they draw near.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:1:2.hebrew: ולא היו צריכים לומר ונכפר להם הדם - כלומר, ונכפר דכתיב בקרא לאו אוענו ואמרו קאי, שיהא אף זה בכלל אמירה, אלא מילתא באנפי נפשה היא, שרוח הקודש בישר את ישראל ע"י משה רבינו: לכשיעשו כן, ונכפר להם הדם:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:1:2.english: And they did not have to recite: "And the blood shall be forgiven for them" - That is to say, "And [it] shall be forgiven," which is written in the verse, does not refer to "And they shall answer and say" [such] that this too would be included in the recitation; rather, it is a matter in its own right, that the Divine Spirit informed Israel through Moses our Teacher: when they do so, "the blood shall be forgiven for them."

Rashi on Sotah 46a:20:1.english: Pulling of a yoke - To disqualify [an animal] regarding the heifer [whose neck is broken].

Rashi on Sotah 46a:22:1.english: That does not produce fruit - A heifer in its first year has not given birth.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:22:2.english: In a place that does not produce fruit - [This refers to] a hard nachal eitan [rough, uncultivated valley].

Rashi on Sotah 46a:22:3.english: Whom they did not allow - For they killed him.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:2:1.hebrew: עגלה - בת שנתה היא, ואם עברה שנתה פסולה, דכל מקום שנאמר בתורה "עגל" סתם, בן שנה הוא, דיליף מ"ועגל וכבש בן שנה":
Rashi on Sotah 46a:2:1.english: A heifer - It is in its first year, and if it has passed its [first] year, it is disqualified; for wherever "calf" is stated in the Torah without specification, it is one year old, as it is derived from "and a calf and a lamb of the first year" [Leviticus 9:3].

Rashi on Sotah 46a:2:2.english: A red heifer - There is no limit to its years.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:2:3.hebrew: מום פוסל בה - דכתיב בפרה אדומה: "אין בה מום" (במדבר יט):
Rashi on Sotah 46a:2:3.english: A blemish disqualifies it - As it is written regarding the red heifer: "there is no blemish in it" (Numbers 19).

Rashi on Sotah 46a:3:1.hebrew: אלא מעתה - דכל היכא דכתב בה מיעוטא הוא, ולא גמרינן מיניה בקל וחומר:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:3:1.english: However, if that is so - that wherever [Scripture] writes bah ["with it"], it is an exclusion, and we do not derive from it via an a fortiori inference.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:3:2.hebrew: לא יהו שאר עבודות פוסלות - בפרה, דהא עול בלבד כתיב בה, אלא דגמר לה בק"ו מעגלה, דכתיב (דברים כא) אשר לא עובד בה, כל עבודות במשמע. ואי בה מיעוטא, לא נגמר מיניה:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:3:2.english: Other labors should not disqualify - [I.e.,] the [red] heifer, for only a yoke is written regarding it; rather, it is derived through an a fortiori inference from the heifer [whose neck is broken], regarding which it is written (Deuteronomy 21[:3]): "Which has not been worked with [bah]" — all labors are implied. And if "bah" is an exclusion, we would not derive [this] from it.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:4:1.hebrew: אלמה אמר רב יהודה הניח - על פרה עודה של שקין — אגודה של שקין — פסולה, ואע"ג דלאו עול הוא, ובעלייה לחודיה מיפסלא, כדכתיב בפרה במלאכת עול האמורה בה: ״אשר לא עלה״ — בעלייה לחודה, ואפילו שלא משכה:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:4:1.english: Why did Rav Yehuda say: [If] he placed - upon a [red] heifer a bundle [udah] of sacks — [meaning] a pack of sacks — it is disqualified, even though it is not a yoke, and it is disqualified by [a burden] merely coming up [upon it], as it is written regarding the [red] heifer, concerning the labor of a yoke stated about it: “which has not come up [upon it]” [Numbers 19:2] — by merely coming up [upon it], even though it did not pull.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:4:2.hebrew: ובעגלה עד שתמשך - שתטלטל המשא מעט, דבעגלה כתיב "אשר לא משכה". ולקמן פריך: כיון דשאר עבודות בפרה לא כתיבי ומעגלה ילפינן, אמאי מיפסל בעלייה לחודה דשאר משאוי שאינו עול ממש? מ"מ שמע מינה דגמר פרה מעגלה בק"ו בשאר עבודות, ואע"ג דכתיב בה מיעוטא:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:4:2.english: And for a heifer, until it pulls - [That is,] that it moves the load slightly, for regarding the heifer [whose neck is broken] it is written, "that has not pulled." And later [the Gemara] asks: Since other labors are not written regarding the red heifer, and we derive [them] from the heifer [whose neck is broken], why is [the red heifer] disqualified by mere placing [of a burden] in the case of other loads that are not an actual yoke? In any event, learn from this that [Rav] derives the red heifer from the heifer [whose neck is broken] via an a fortiori inference regarding other labors, even though an exclusion is written regarding it.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:4:3.hebrew: שאני פרה דילפינן עול עול - וכיון דגזירה שוה מופנה היא, הוה ליה כמאן דכתיב בגופה, ומיעוטא דבה דריש ליה לדרשא אחרינא, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:4:3.english: A [red] heifer is different, as we derive “yoke” “yoke” - And since it is a free verbal analogy [gezerah shavah], it is as though it were written in [the passage of the red heifer] itself; and the exclusion [derived from the word] “bah” [“with it”] is expounded for a different exposition, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:5:1.english: A heifer should also be derived [via] “yoke,” “yoke” from a [red] heifer - With respect to a blemish.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:6:1.hebrew: למעוטי קדשים דלא פסלה בהו עבודה - מהקרבה, אבל פרה לא ממעטא, דאתיא מג"ש:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:6:1.english: To exclude sacred [offerings], which are not disqualified by labor - From being offered [on the altar]; however, the [red] heifer is not excluded, as it is derived from a verbal analogy [gezeira shava].

Rashi on Sotah 46a:7:1.hebrew: מי ליכא דפסלי בהו שנים - והרי פסח וחטאת דכתיב בהו "בני שנתן". וכי איצטריך בה למעטינהו מפסול עבודה, להכי איצטריך, דאי לא מעטינהו הוו גמרי בקל וחומר מעגלה:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:7:1.english: Are there none that are disqualified by years - Behold, [there are] the Paschal offering and the sin-offering, regarding which it is written "within their [first] year." And when [the verse] is needed in this [matter] to exclude them from disqualification by labor, it is for this [purpose] that it is needed; for if it had not excluded them, they would have been derived through an a fortiori inference from [the] heifer [whose neck is broken].

Rashi on Sotah 46a:8:1.english: We read [the text as]: “[that] have been used for labor.”

Rashi on Sotah 46a:8:2.english: Prohibited labor - For example, on Shabbat, or [working with] diverse kinds with an ox and a donkey.

Rashi on Sotah 46a:9:1.hebrew: עבודת איסור נמי מהאי קרא נפקא - דכיון דתרי קראי כתיבי, על כרחיך חד מינייהו לעבודת איסור:
Rashi on Sotah 46a:9:1.english: Prohibited labor is also derived from this verse - For since two verses are written, perforce one of them [is] for prohibited labor.
